slides.title: The IDS flagged 6 servers. The pcap had 15 domains.
slides.sub: How I scoped an infection from one 14-minute packet capture in Wireshark.

slides.title: The alert
body: 6+ alerts: **ET MALWARE FormBook CnC Checkin (GET)**, to 6 IPs on port 80.
First question: which internal host talked to them?
slides.caption: Statistics → Conversations, limited to the six alerted IPs. Every row is 172.16.8[.]49.

slides.title: Prove it with zero
body: Same filter, but exclude that host:

slides.title: Who uses the host
bullets: Each fact checked in a second protocol
slides.caption: Frame 2816: Kerberos AS-REP for rvance.

slides.title: A machine, not a person
body: 131 HTTP requests to 15 domains. Each domain gets its own random 4-character path.
About 24 s per domain, then the whole list again after ~6 min.

slides.title: Pivot on behavior, not alerts
body: Every C2 request says **Firefox 39 on Windows 8**, a 2015 browser. The real browser on this host is Edge 151.
That User-Agent matches the same 131 requests. Two methods, same traffic.

slides.title: Same data, 14 times
body: Each of the 14 suspicious domains got the same **283,087 bytes** of POST data per visit. About 4.5 MB in total.
Tip: the Length column shows one TCP segment. Use `http.content_length`.

slides.title: A decoy in the list
body: www.independent[.]ie is a real news site. It answered like one: 301 to HTTPS.
13 of the other 14 domains were registered 72 to 156 days before the incident.

slides.title: Verdict: true positive, high confidence
bullets: **Reset** rvance's passwords, including ones saved in the browser
**Block** the 14 suspicious domains by domain, not by Cloudflare IP
**Hunt** for the Firefox 39 User-Agent on every other host

slides.title: What I took from it
bullets: Alerts showed 6 of 15 domains. Behavior found all of them.
Measure time gaps with a column. Don't estimate.
Finish enrichment before you call a domain a decoy.
